headline: 463 killed in 532 road accidents in June, report says
summary: A Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity report reveals a staggering death toll from road, rail, and waterway accidents across the country in a single month.
details: At least 463 people were killed and 1,323 others injured in 532 road accidents across Bangladesh in June, according to a report by Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity.

The overall tragedy was even higher when including rail and waterway accidents. A total of 590 accidents across all three modes of transport killed 513 people and injured 1,336 others during the month.
Motorcycle accidents were particularly deadly, accounting for 32.33% of all road crashes. These crashes killed 173 people and injured 132.
Chattogram division recorded the highest number of road accidents with 128 crashes, while Mymensingh division saw the fewest with 25.
The victims included a wide range of people, including 111 drivers, 71 pedestrians, 60 students, 47 children, and 45 women.
The report cited several factors for these accidents, including unchecked movement of motorcycles and easy-bikes on highways, lack of road signs and streetlights, and faulty highway construction.
Other contributing factors included traffic law violations, wrong-way driving, unskilled drivers, unfit vehicles, and potholes formed during rains.
The Jatri Kalyan Samity's Accident Monitoring Cell noted that actual casualty figures could be significantly higher as many incidents go unreported in newspapers.

headline: HSC candidates postpone all board exams in Chittagong protest
summary: Students are demanding the postponement of exams due to flood-hit areas and errors in question papers, threatening to launch a movement for the Education Minister's resignation.
details: Over 200 HSC candidates gathered in front of the Chittagong Education Board in Muradpur on Tuesday morning to demand the postponement of all education board exams across the country.
The students argued that many candidates in flood-affected areas cannot reach their exam centers due to severe waterlogging and disasters, making it unfair to continue the exams.

Beyond the postponement, the protesters demanded punishment for those responsible for errors in the question papers and the immediate replacement of registration cards and admit cards lost in the floods.
The protest caused significant traffic congestion on CDA Avenue, blocking traffic from Gate 2 toward Bahaddarhat for several hours.
Board Secretary Mohammad Zahirul Huq assured the students that an inter-board committee would decide on the punishment for those involved in question paper errors.
He also stated that the board is taking immediate action to provide new admit cards to students whose documents were destroyed by the flood waters.
Law enforcement agencies remained on high alert at the scene to maintain order during the demonstration.
Students warned that if their demands are not met, they will launch a larger movement demanding the resignation of the Education Minister.
caption:
HSC students take to the streets in Chittagong, demanding a total halt to exams due to floods and question paper errors.

Over 200 HSC candidates gathered in front of the Chittagong Education Board in Muradpur on Tuesday morning to demand the postponement of all education board exams across the country.

The students argued that many candidates in flood-affected areas cannot reach their exam centers due to severe waterlogging and disasters, making it unfair to continue the exams.

Beyond the postponement, the protesters demanded punishment for those responsible for errors in the question papers and the immediate replacement of registration cards and admit cards lost in the floods.

The protest caused significant traffic congestion on CDA Avenue, blocking traffic from Gate 2 toward Bahaddarhat for several hours.

Board Secretary Mohammad Zahirul Huq assured the students that an inter-board committee would decide on the punishment for those involved in question paper errors.

He also stated that the board is taking immediate action to provide new admit cards to students whose documents were destroyed by the flood waters.

Law enforcement agencies remained on high alert at the scene to maintain order during the demonstration.

Students warned that if their demands are not met, they will launch a larger movement demanding the resignation of the Education Minister.
